memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses did everything just as the Lord commanded him. So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year." - Exod 40:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Moses did everything just as the Lord commanded him." That sentence, in various forms, will appear seven more times before this chapter ends.

Scripture is not being repetitive by accident. It is underlining the one thing that made this day possible: complete obedience.

And notice the date. The first day of the first month in the second year — one year and two weeks after Israel walked out of Egypt.

Think about what that year contained. The Red Sea. Bitter water. Manna. Sinai. The golden calf. Broken tablets. Three thousand dead. Renewed covenant. Months of building.

A year of extraordinary highs and devastating failures. And at the end of it, a tabernacle standing in the desert with God's people gathered around it.

That is encouraging for anyone looking back on a year they would rather forget. God was not finished with Israel after the calf, and He is not finished with you.

The Christian life is not a straight upward line. It includes failure, repentance, restoration and slow rebuilding. What matters is not that the year was clean but that God was faithful through it.

Look at where you were a year ago. God has been working.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has the last year held for you — and where has God been in it?
2. Has a failure made you assume God's purposes for you are finished?
3. Where do you need to obey completely rather than partially?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Your faithfulness through a year I could not have navigated alone. Help me obey You fully. Amen.
